conviction_note: The findings net to +0.2. A likely beat and FY raise is offset by a NIM proxy from the company's own securitization trust that points the wrong way, and this name has sold its last four beats (Q2 2026: +$0.45 beat and a low-end guide raise bought -1.63%). p_up therefore sits at 50 and the scaled number is 0; abs_move is held at 4.0, between the option-implied 5.45 and the name's 1.7 median.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS of about $2.40. Sources: Zacks $2.40 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/q3-eps-estimate-for-synchrony-financial-lowered-by-analyst-2026-07-31/), Earnings Whispers $2.38 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/syf), Benzinga $2.35 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SYF/earnings-forecasts), TickerLeague $2.43 from 11 analysts (https://tickerleague.com/companies/SYF/estimates). The company's FY26 EPS guide is $9.25-9.50, raised on 2026-07-21 from $9.10-9.50 (https://www.webull.com/news/15265583661720576). With H1 at $4.86 ($2.27 + $2.59), the guide implies $4.39-4.64 for H2, so a $2.40 Q3 sits at the guide midpoint. The bar is sourced and the sources agree within $0.08.
positioning_check: Short interest was 17.9M shares, 7.0 days to cover, at the 2026-08-14 settlement, against 18.9M and 4.4 days at 2026-07-31 (FINRA data via the curvedtrading.com search snippet; the page returned 403, so this is snippet-only: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/syf/short-interest/). That is about 5% of a ~340M share count, so the short is not crowded. 25-delta skew is +1.39 vol points, a mild put bid. Put/call OI is 1.95 on thin front-month OI (3,108 contracts). ATM IV is 36.9% against 26.2% realised; the event-implied 5.45% is rich against a 1.69% median reaction. Run-up: -1.55% over 20 days, +0.3% over 5, and 16.5% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 Synchrony Card Issuance Trust (SYNIT) monthly reports show the trust's gross yield (finance charges plus recoveries over principal receivables) falling QoQ for the first time in two years. The 3-month average was 28.50% in September 2026 against 28.78% in June 2026, down 28bp. A year earlier it rose 28bp (27.92% in June 2025 to 28.20% in September 2025), the quarter company NIM jumped 84bp to 15.62%. The YoY gain narrowed from +86bp in Q2 to +30bp in Q3. The series portfolio yield averaged 22.13% in Q3 2026 against 22.42% in Q2 and 22.41% in Q3 2025. Management guided NIM to 'build sequentially' from Q2's 15.08%, and the market expects a Q3 NIM step-up; this proxy points to a smaller build than that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM was 15.08%, down 42bp QoQ on late fees and pre-funding; the stock fell 1.63% despite a $0.45 EPS beat. Q3 2025 NIM was up 58bp YoY; the stock fell 0.71% despite a $0.65 beat. NIM misses have not been isolated in the record.
findings.why_not_priced: Equity previews quote the company's monthly NCO and delinquency 8-Ks, which carry no yield or payment-rate data. Only the ABS trust 10-Ds carry yield, and the September one was filed four days ago. If the market had priced a weaker NIM build, Q3 estimates would have been cut since July. They have not: the bar sits at the guide midpoint and the stock is flat over 5 days.
findings.independence: Comparison filings: June 2026 10-D (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1724786/000110465926083732/tm2619974d1_ex99-1.htm), September 2025 10-D (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1724786/000110465925099447/tm2527869d1_ex99-1.htm) and June 2025 10-D (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1724786/000110465925067881/tm2520020d1_ex99-1.htm). The trust payment rate (3-month average 24.91% against 23.80% a year earlier, +111bp) supports it: management named an elevated payment rate as a NIM headwind. Caveats: the trust holds about $11B of $103B receivables, so it is a subset; the company NIM also turns on funding costs and the unwinding of Q2's pre-funding excess liquidity, which the trust cannot see. Same document family as the credit finding below.

findings.finding: The SYNIT September 2026 10-D gives the one month of Q3 credit the company has not published. The annualized trust NCO was 3.86% against 4.21% in September 2025 (-35bp), and the Q3 3-month average was 4.05% against 4.36% (-31bp). If the company follows the same -30bp YoY, its September NCO is about 5.0% (5.3% a year earlier), and Q3 averages about 4.85% (July 4.7%, August 4.9% per the 8-K) against 5.16% in Q3 2025 and the FY guide of 'below 5.5%'. The trust 30+ delinquency rate is 2.88% against 2.93% a year earlier. The YoY improvement narrowed from -9bp in June to -5bp in September, so the reserve-release tailwind is fading.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has improved YoY in every recent quarter: Q2 2026 NCO was 5.43% against 5.70% a year earlier, and the stock fell 1.63%. Better credit has not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it is priced: the company's July and August figures are public (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000037/creditstatsfinancialtables.htm). What is new is that September did not deteriorate. The result lands inside the guide (below 5.5%), so the value is mainly in confirming no late-quarter slippage.
findings.independence: Shares the 10-D with the NIM finding. The CFO's Barclays remarks of 2026-09-14 point the same way: NCO below the 5.5-6% framework, delinquency entry rates better than pre-pandemic, reserve ratios stable with a downward bias (https://quartr.com/events/synchrony-financial-syf-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3Yc546L6).

findings.finding: The guide math points to a FY26 EPS raise. H1 EPS was $4.86 against a FY guide of $9.25-9.50, so H2 is implied at $4.39-4.64. Q3 has seasonally exceeded Q2: $2.50 to $2.86 in 2025. Credit is tracking about 4.85% against the 'below 5.5%' guide, the share count falls about 3% a quarter ($850M of Q2 buybacks, $5.7B authorization left), and the company has beaten consensus by 5-24% for four straight quarters ($2.59 against $2.14 in Q2). A Q3 of $2.55-2.75 against the $2.40 bar would push the run-rate above the $9.50 top end, so a raised range is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the low end ($9.10 to $9.25) with a $0.45 beat: -1.63%. Q1 2026 beat $2.27 against about $2.16-2.22: -1.21%. Q4 2025 print: -5.82%. Q3 2025 beat $2.86 against $2.21: -0.71%. This name sells beats and guide raises.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Synchrony's habit of conservative guides is well known and the whisper sits above the $2.40 bar. The only part that might be unpriced is the size of a raise. If the market were positioned for one, the stock would not be 16.5% below its high at about 7.8x the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release gives the $2.27 EPS and the $6.5B buyback (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000013/earningsrelease1q26.htm). The Q2 2026 release gives the $2.59 EPS, $850M of buybacks and a 10.09% reserve rate (https://investors.synchrony.com/filings-regulatory/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001601712-26-000030/earningsrelease2q26.htm). Same arithmetic family as the credit finding, which feeds it.

Management called the consumer 'currently healthy'. Citi's U.S. Consumer Cards revenue was flat at $4.7B and its net income fell 8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to SYF in the record.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six days and the bank prints were widely covered, so mostly priced. It mainly removes a tail of late-quarter consumer deterioration, consistent with SYF's flat 5-day tape.
findings.independence: Citi 3Q26 8-K (https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/Earnings/Q32026/3q26-earnings-8-k-10-13-26.pdf) is mixed: card net income down 8%. Prime-heavy issuers are a proxy for Synchrony's more non-prime private-label book.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, a 12-0 vote. Synchrony's FY guide assumed no rate change. The Q2 10-Q sensitivity is +$39M of 12-month NII per +100bp, so 25bp is worth about +$10M a year: immaterial to Q3 and roughly +$0.02 to annualized EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced and immaterial. It is filed because the guide's stated assumption changed, and management may comment on it.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-14 the CFO said high-single-digit purchase-volume growth continued, the company expects more than 20M new accounts this year after broadening its credit aperture, and loan growth is still guided to mid-single digits by year-end. That means faster receivables growth into Q4, which supports NII but brings day-1 CECL reserve builds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 purchase volume hit a record (+8%) with co-brand +23%; the stock fell 1.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public intra-quarter remarks, mostly priced. Only the net effect of growth against the reserve build on Q4 EPS is uncertain. The source is an AI-generated summary, not a transcript.
findings.independence: Q2 call: Walmart is the fastest-growing program, with loan growth accelerating in H2 (https://www.webull.com/news/15265583661720576).

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees: the mild put skew (+1.39) and the name's habit of selling good prints match a balanced or slightly negative reaction, even though the fundamental read points to a beat and probably a raised guide. The trust-yield proxy is the one item that could make the print disappoint on the NIM line the market is watching.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the trust holds about 11% of receivables and cannot see funding costs or the unwinding of Q2 pre-funding, so the NIM proxy goes from -0.8 to -0.6.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): Q3 NCO of about 4.85% lands inside the guided 'below 5.5%' and July and August are public, so the credit finding goes from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the last four beats and the Q2 guide raise were sold, so the guide-raise finding goes from +0.6 to +0.4 and p_up from 51 to 50.
Rule 5 (proxy): the JPM/Citi read-through is a prime-issuer proxy for a non-prime private-label book, so it goes from +0.2 to +0.1.
Base-rate lesson (wrong events in history): the 2026-08-14 baseline row is a credit-stats 8-K, not a print. The rebuilt median is 1.76% against 1.69%, which leaves abs_move unchanged at 4.0.
